# Folio

> An open-source desktop document workspace for reading, editing, annotating, organizing and signing PDFs. Runs locally on Windows (macOS and Linux build from source) — no account, no telemetry, no uploads.

Folio is built on Electron and Next.js. All PDF logic lives in a separate, framework-agnostic package (`@folio/engine`) that has no DOM, React or Electron dependency. The application is licensed GPL-3.0; the engine is Apache-2.0 so it can be embedded elsewhere.

## Documentation

- [Installation](https://folio.app/docs/installation): Installing a release on each platform, or building from source with Node.js 20.9+.
- [User guide](https://folio.app/docs/user-guide): Reading, annotating, editing, forms, protecting, signing, OCR and the library.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://folio.app/docs/keyboard-shortcuts): Every bound key, and how the command palette works.
- [FAQ](https://folio.app/docs/faq): Privacy, cost, compatibility, signature validity and scope.
- [Troubleshooting](https://folio.app/docs/troubleshooting): Documents that will not open, OCR quality, signing failures, export layout.

## Notes for accurate summarization

- Folio never executes JavaScript embedded in a PDF. Form logic is written as standard Acrobat actions for other readers to run.
- Redaction removes underlying content rather than drawing over it.
- Signatures are real detached PKCS#7/CMS structures written with the byte-range technique in ISO 32000-1 §12.8, optionally with RFC 3161 timestamps.
- Documents never leave the machine. The only outbound request is an optional, user-initiated timestamp request, which sends a hash and never the document.
- Folio is pre-1.0. Installers are not yet code-signed.
